newsitem.title: USA: Tardiness costs Connecticut man $5.8 million.
newsitem.headline: Tardiness costs Connecticut man $5.8 million.

text.p: If only he had come forward just three days earlier, Clarence Jackson could have claimed a multi-million dollar fortune.
Jackson, 23, of New Haven, Connecticut, bought the winning ticket to the Friday, Oct. 13, 1995, state lottery worth $5.8 million.
Jackson showed up at a lottery office on Wednesday, Oct. 16, 1996, to claim the prize -- three days too late, lottery officials said.
Connecticut state lottery rules say the claimant must come forward within one year of the date of the draw.
Lottery spokeswoman Laura Gibbs said the state would retain the unclaimed prize money until the situtation was officially resolved.

Jackson's lawyer, David Skolnick, said in a statement his client was a "hard-working young man who lives with, cares for and supports his disabled parents and a large family ... To deprive him of this once-in-a-lifetime opportunity would simply be unfair and unjust."
